newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran says may expose Germany-Iraq arms ties.
newsitem.headline: Iran says may expose Germany-Iraq arms ties.

text.p: Iran said on Friday it might release documents on alleged German help in making Iraqi chemical weapons because a German court has accused Iranian leaders of ordering the killing of four Kurdish dissidents in Berlin.

"The judiciary has received and is following up complaints...The main point is that, based on United Nations documents and some publications, Germany was directly involved in the production of Iraqi chemical weapons," judiciary head Ayatollah Mohammad Yazdi said.
"We did not want to go public with these cases as we were willing to maintain good relations but unfortunately (Germany's) government has begun to be involved," Yazdi said on Tehran radio.
German prosecutors on Friday demanded life sentences for an Iranian and a Lebanese, after accusing Tehran of ordering the deaths of three Kurdish opposition leaders and their translator in 1992.

Yazdi said the German government was cooperating with the court "under the influence of America, Israel, England and opposition groups who are unwilling to see improvement in Iran- Germany and Iran-Europe relations".
Iran has denied any role in the killings and protested to Germany on Thursday over the charges.
Several hundred Iranians protested on Friday in front of the German embassy in Tehran, which was protected by dozens of police, journalists said.
Germany tightened export controls in 1992 after revelations that some German firms had helped Iraq develop rockets and chemical weapons.
